qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Rigorous rail safety homologation, proprietary signaling software, and a large global installed fleet create meaningful barriers to entry. However, primary rolling stock manufacturing suffers from fierce competitive bidding by state-backed transit authorities, leaving margins razor-thin. Value destruction from the 2021 Bombardier Transportation acquisition resulted in severe execution losses, multi-year negative free cash flow, and 5-year GAAP ROIC well below 5% (near zero/negative).
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3 (3b=N, REJECT). Alstom is the world's #2 rail manufacturer, but rolling stock production is characterized by fierce public-tender bidding and zero pricing power. The value-destructive Bombardier acquisition led to massive cash burn (€-557M FCF in FY24), sub-5% ROIC, and an emergency €1B dilutive rights issue in mid-2024 to defend its investment-grade rating.
qualitative.evidence: Bombardier Transportation integration led to multi-year operating losses and negative free cash flow (€-557M in FY2023/24). Net debt escalated to ~€3B before being rescued via a €1B rights issue and €750M hybrid bond in 2024. Multi-cycle GAAP ROIC is structurally below 5%, far below the 12% Munger bar.
